title: The Metropole Cafe scene
summary: Moore describes the crowds and the double bands at the Metropole.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Was he called the Judge then, did he have that nickname at that time, The Judge?

And we alternated with the Gay '90s lady singers, we had the jazz. And after a while the whole place -- got rid of the Gay '90s and we hired another jazz band, there were two bands alternating and the joint was jumping because up on the second floor was another joint, they had Gene Krupa up there and we had Charlie Shavers up there, oh, there was big
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
names during that time, Juliet Prowse, you could say the joint was jumping.
Did you have a young crowd pretty much or did you have all ages?
We had all kinds, we had tourists from all over the country that come into New York, they'd all come into the Metropole, the place was filled up to the mim all the time.
And they used to open it out on the street, too, at one time, anyway.
Yeah, right. And I was in and out of the Metropole, one time I was there with Coleman Hawkins, Roy Eldridge and different, different -- (Recording interruption)
